explanation: The kubelet was unable to mount the required volume for the pod.

pattern: CNI plugin failed to set up pod network
root_cause: The Container Network Interface (CNI) plugin failed to configure the network namespace for the pod, often due to CNI daemon failures, IP address exhaustion, or node-level configuration errors.
explanation: This error occurs when the kubelet attempts to provision a pod sandbox but the CNI plugin is unable to allocate an IP address or set up the network routing interface. This halts pod initialization, leaving the pod stuck in ContainerCreating.
recommendations: Check the status and logs of the CNI DaemonSet pods (e.g., aws-node, calico-node, flannel, cilium) in the kube-system namespace.
Verify if the subnet or IP Address Management (IPAM) pool has exhausted all available IP addresses.
Inspect the CNI configuration directory (/etc/cni/net.d/) on the affected node for missing or malformed configuration files.
Restart the CNI daemon pod running on the affected Kubernetes node to trigger re-initialization.

root_cause: Kubernetes failed to create the pod sandbox.
explanation: The kubelet was unable to create the pod sandbox, commonly due to CNI or container runtime issues.
